newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Cairo Bank and USCB announce merger.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Cairo Bank and USCB announce merger.

text.p: The boards of United Saudi Commercial Bank (USCB) and Saudi Cairo Bank (SCB) agreed to merge into a new bank, a USBC statement said on Monday.
It said USBC would issue 2.5 million bonus shares to its current shareholders ahead of the merger, on the basis of one bonus share for each four held.
The statement did not name the new bank, but said the merger would involve shareholders of the two banks getting one share in the new bank for each one they own in USCB and SCB.
"Shareholders of the two merged banks will receive one share in the the newly founded bank for each share held," it said.

Saudi Cairo Bank is 25 percent owned by the Saudi government's Public Investment Fund and Egypt's Banque du Caire holds 20 percent. In June 1996, Saudi billionaire Prince al-Waleed bin Talal and 15 other Saudi investors acquired 33.4 percent of SCB, becoming the majority shareholders.
Other Saudi investors hold the rest in the bank, which in February reported 1996 profits of 178.3 million riyals ($47.5 million) from 212.1 million riyals in 1995.
USBC -- mostly owned by Prince al-Waleed and other Saudi investors -- said its 1996 profits were up 10.6 percent to 340 million riyals.
